key_insight: Lead-free AgBiS2 memristors can switch at ultra-low voltage and be tuned from abrupt digital to gradual analog behavior by controlling interfacial and thickness-driven filament evolution.
engineering_relevance: The work points to sustainable, solution-processable memristors with synaptic-like conductance modulation for neuromorphic hardware while avoiding toxic lead.
method: First-principles calculations identified favorable Ag interstitial defects and low Ag migration barriers.
Interface and thickness engineering were used to tune switching from digital to analog.
Electrical pulse tests and impedance spectroscopy probed ionic-electronic coupling and synaptic response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~0.08 V SET voltage, ON/OFF ratios above 10^4, and gradual conductance modulation under pulse trains, supported by post-operando structural changes.
watch_item: Repeated filament formation and rupture causes substantial morphological evolution, which may affect durability and switching variability over long-term operation.
paper_title: Controlling Switching Evolution in Lead-Free Perovskite-Inspired Chalcogenide Memristors for Neuromorphic Computing
